component.name: FerrumKix
component.summary: Desktop music player with album-grouped playlists and Audio CD support
Musikspieler mit nach Alben geordneten Wiedergabelisten und Audio-CD-Unterstuetzung

description.p: FerrumKix is a dark, tidy music player for the desktop. The cover art and details of the current track sit on the left, the playlist grouped by album on the right, the transport controls at the bottom.

ul.li: Plays MP3, FLAC, OGG, Opus, M4A, AAC, WAV, WavPack, APE, WMA and more
Reads artist, album, year, duration, sample rate, bitrate and embedded cover art
Groups the playlist by folder, with collapsible album headers
Quick search across title, artist, album and file name
Drag and drop of files and whole folders
Shuffle, repeat and gapless playback
Integrated conversion to MP3, FLAC and Ogg Vorbis, including ordered album output
Automatically detects inserted Audio CDs on Linux and shows them as a separate playlist
Browses and plays albums from a configured Lyrion Media Server
Edits common MP3 album metadata and embedded cover art
MPRIS integration for media keys, desktop controls and notifications
Accent colour, font size and per-screen scaling on Linux

description.p: FerrumKix ist ein dunkler, aufgeraeumter Musikspieler fuer den Schreibtisch: links das Titelbild und die Angaben zum laufenden Stueck, rechts die Wiedergabeliste nach Alben geordnet, unten der Transport.

ul.li: The application was renamed from FerrumPlay to FerrumKix; other products already carried the old name.
The application id, the binary, the D-Bus name and the AUR package moved with it, and the old id is declared as replaced.
Settings, playlist and the cover art cache are carried over on the first start.
New application icon.
Converted files are named from a pattern of their own, set in the settings with the placeholders known from tagging.
The pattern holds for files, for a CD rip and for the tracks cut out of a CUE; the extension comes from the chosen format.
Zero padding of the track number is a switch of its own, and a missing number stays empty instead of becoming a zero.
The conversion queue reads like the playlist, with check boxes, group positions and file details.
The application scale moves in single percent, under the pointer and at the wheel.
Three appearances to choose from in the settings: dark, gray dark and gray light.
The player follows the chosen appearance, from the footer deck to the veil over the playlist.
Drop-down lists, menus and list rows change along with it instead of keeping the previous colours.
The MP3 tag editor proposes every empty field on its own: file name for the title, folder name for album and artist.
A missing track number follows the order of the file names; numbers already in the files stay untouched.
The genre box completes what is typed from the genre defaults in the settings.
After a while without input the view returns to the playing track and scrolls along with every following one.
Page up, page down, home and end scroll the playlist even when the focus sits elsewhere.
The filled accent buttons carry dark text again instead of white.
Configure up to three Lyrion Media Servers with separate named tabs and sync targets.
Favorite filtering reports its track count and required sync space; album views show their duration and size.
Save, load and open M3U/M3U8 playlists, including from the command line.
Audio CD views show identified metadata and artwork immediately, and rip targets can use placeholder-based album subfolders.
Existing conversion targets require confirmation before they are overwritten.
Untagged files get a proposal in the MP3 tag editor: numbering, titles from file names, album and artist from the folder.
A cover can be chosen through a file picker, and the drop zone shows what it accepts.
Padding track numbers with zeros now applies to the converter and to split CUE sheets as well.
Ripped MP3s get their tags and file names from the same writer as the tag editor.
A conversion or rip can be cancelled, and the window is covered while one runs.
Tracks can be unchecked in a Lyrion album and are then skipped when playing in FerrumKix.
The application scale takes effect without a restart, and the diagnostic log has a switch in the settings.
FerrumKix can act as a remote control for any player registered with a Lyrion Media Server.
Audio CDs are identified at MusicBrainz, and the details and cover art go into the tags when ripping.
"Refresh library" now asks the Lyrion server to scan for new and changed music first.
Fixed the CD tray closing while a disc was being inserted, shuffle having no effect on a CD, and seeking within a CD track.
Added sorting and a favorites filter to the Lyrion album overview.
Added the favorites sync into a folder of your choosing.
The favorites sync now reports its state and survives leaving the view.
Added Lyrion Media Server album browsing and local HTTP-stream playback.
Added the integrated MP3 tag editor.
Improved Audio CD timing and playlist handling.

description.p: The converter now uses the full selected set of tracks from the playlist context menu.

ul.li: Added the integrated Audio Converter for MP3, FLAC and Ogg Vorbis.
Selections and source folders can be converted to ordered single files.
Added direct Audio-CD ripping through cdparanoia.
Added drag-and-drop reordering and a context menu for tracks and albums in the playlist.
The playlist now visibly follows the shuffled playback order while shuffle is enabled.
The current track is scrolled into view when the player starts.
Added automatic Audio CD detection on Linux, with a separate temporary CD playlist.
Added MPRIS integration, ReplayGain, missing-track handling and single-instance opening.
Opening a track in an existing instance now scrolls the playlist to it.
